title: Review: The periodic table: Classification of elements
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S3.1#c17 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S3.1#c13 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S3.1#c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; S3.1#c16 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: S3.1#q02, S3.1#q03, S3.1#q08, S3.1#q23, S3.1#q24, S3.1#q13, S3.1#q01, S3.1#q27, S3.1#q06, S3.1#q10, S3.1#q12, S3.1#q14, S3.1#q20. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Electronegativity
items.clue: The ability of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons in a covalent bond towards itself.

items.label: Atomic radius
items.clue: Half the distance between the nuclei of two bonded atoms of the same element, usually given in picometres (pm).

items.label: Valence electrons
items.clue: The electrons in the outer (highest occupied) energy level of an atom of a main-group element, which take part in bonding.

items.label: Electron affinity
items.clue: The energy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions: X(g) + e⁻ → X⁻(g).

questions.stem: Gallium (Z = 31) has the electron configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p¹. Which statement classifies gallium correctly?

options.text: A p-block metalloid, as it borders the stepped metal/non-metal line
A p-block non-metal, as metals are in the s- and d-blocks
A d-block element, as each atom holds a filled 3d sublevel
A p-block metal, as its last electron enters the 4p sublevel

questions.explanation: The block is named after the sublevel being filled in the aufbau order. After zinc the 3d sublevel is full, and gallium's last electron enters 4p, so gallium is the first p-block element of period 4 (group 13). It lies below and to the left of the stepped line, and is a metal: shiny and an electrical conductor.

questions.stem: Selenium is in period 4 and group 16 of the periodic table. Which statement about a selenium atom is correct?

options.text: It has sixteen valence electrons, in the fourth energy level
It has four valence electrons, located in the sixth energy level
It has six valence electrons, in the fourth energy level
It has only two valence electrons, in the fourth energy level

questions.explanation: Period 4 means the outer electrons are in the fourth energy level; group 16 means 16 − 10 = 6 valence electrons. The configuration is [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁴, with 4s² 4p⁴ in the outer level.

questions.stem: How does the first ionization energy of rubidium (Z = 37) compare with that of sodium (Z = 11)?

options.text: Higher, as rubidium's nucleus carries a much larger positive charge
Lower, as rubidium's outer electron is further out and more shielded
Equal, as each atom loses one electron to gain a noble-gas configuration
Lower, as rubidium's nuclear attraction is shared among more electrons

questions.explanation: Rubidium's outer electron is in the fifth energy level, sodium's in the third. The greater distance and the extra shielding by inner electrons outweigh the larger nuclear charge, so less energy is needed (Rb 403 kJ mol⁻¹, Na 496 kJ mol⁻¹).

questions.stem: Small pieces of lithium and of potassium are added separately to cold water. How does the reaction of potassium compare with that of lithium, and why?

options.text: More vigorous, as its outer electron is further out and more shielded
Less vigorous, as its larger nuclear charge holds its outer electron more tightly
Equally vigorous, as both are group 1 metals with one outer electron
More vigorous, as its nuclear attraction is shared among more electrons

questions.stem: Which statement about aluminium oxide, Al₂O₃, is correct?

options.text: It reacts with acids only, as every metal oxide is basic
It reacts with bases only, as it is a p-block non-metal oxide
It reacts with neither acids nor bases, being neutral
It reacts with both acids and bases, since it is amphoteric

questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide is amphoteric: it reacts with acids, for example Al₂O₃(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2AlCl₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l), and also with bases such as sodium hydroxide. In period 3 it lies between the basic oxides of sodium and magnesium and the acidic oxides of the non-metals.

questions.stem: What is the oxidation state of nitrogen in the nitrite ion?
questions.explanation: Nitrite is NO₂⁻. With oxygen −2 and the sum equal to the ion's charge: x + 2(−2) = −1, so x = +3. This matches the rule that the '-ite' ion has the lower oxidation state.

questions.stem: Which element is classified as a metalloid?

options.text: Silicon
Aluminium
Iodine
Scandium

questions.explanation: Silicon lies on the stepped line between metals and non-metals and has intermediate properties: it is a shiny solid but a semiconductor, and its oxide is acidic. The metalloids are boron, silicon, germanium, arsenic, antimony and tellurium.

questions.stem: An atom has the electron configuration [Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p³. Which statement gives the group of the element correctly?

options.text: Group 5, as its outer level holds five valence electrons
Group 15, as its 4p³ electrons place it in the third p-block column
Group 12, as its full 3d sublevel places it in the d-block
Group 4, as its outer electrons occupy the fourth energy level

questions.explanation: The configuration ends in 4p³, so the element is in period 4 and in the third column of the p-block. With groups numbered 1 to 18, the p-block is groups 13 to 18, so it is group 15 (arsenic, Z = 33); it has 2 + 3 = 5 valence electrons, and 5 + 10 = 15.

questions.stem: The ions Na⁺, F⁻, Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ all have the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶. Which lists them in order of decreasing ionic radius?

options.text: O²⁻ > F⁻ > Na⁺ > Mg²⁺
O²⁻ = F⁻ = Na⁺ = Mg²⁺
Mg²⁺ > Na⁺ > F⁻ > O²⁻
Na⁺ > Mg²⁺ > O²⁻ > F⁻

questions.explanation: All four ions have the same 10 electrons in the same arrangement, so size depends on nuclear charge: 8, 9, 11 and 12 protons. The greater the nuclear charge acting on the same electrons, the more strongly they are pulled in, so radius decreases from O²⁻ to Mg²⁺.

questions.stem: Bromine water is added separately to aqueous potassium chloride and to aqueous potassium iodide. Which observation is expected?

options.text: A reaction occurs with the potassium chloride only
There is no reaction with either of the two solutions
A reaction occurs with both of the salt solutions
A reaction occurs with the potassium iodide only

questions.explanation: Bromine oxidizes iodide ions, which are below it in group 17: Br₂(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Br⁻(aq) + I₂(aq), and the solution darkens to brown. Bromine cannot oxidize chloride ions, because chlorine attracts electrons more strongly than bromine.

questions.stem: Which statement about ocean acidification is correct?

options.text: Dissolved CO₂ forms carbonic acid, lowering the pH, but seawater stays alkaline
Seawater has now become acidic, with a pH below 7, because of absorbed CO₂
Acid rain falling on the sea is the main cause of the fall in seawater pH
Warmer seawater dissolves more CO₂, which is the main reason the pH is falling

questions.explanation: CO₂(g) + H₂O(l) ⇌ H₂CO₃(aq), and carbonic acid releases H⁺ ions. The average surface pH has fallen from about 8.2 to about 8.1 since pre-industrial times: seawater is less alkaline, not acidic.

questions.stem: What are the oxidation states of hydrogen in sodium hydride, NaH, and of oxygen in sodium peroxide, Na₂O₂?
questions.explanation: In NaH, sodium is +1, so hydrogen is −1 (a metal hydride contains H⁻). In Na₂O₂, 2(+1) + 2x = 0, so oxygen is −1 (the peroxide ion O₂²⁻).

questions.stem: Manganese forms compounds in oxidation states from +2 to +7. Which statement explains why transition elements show variable oxidation states?

options.text: They lose different numbers of electrons, each ion reaching a stable noble-gas configuration
Their 3d electrons, filled last, are the outermost and are removed first in any number
Each oxidation state leaves a half-filled or filled d sublevel, which has special stability
Their 4s and 3d electrons are close in energy, so successive ionization energies are close in value
